newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo prosecutors indict ex-Nomura officials.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo prosecutors indict ex-Nomura officials.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors said on Wednesday that two former Nomura Securities Co Ltd directors had been indicted for giving 49.7 million yen to racketeer Ryoichi Koike in March 1995 in violation of the Japan's securities and exchange law and the commercial code.

The prosecutors said that the two -- Shimpei Matsuki, who was in charge of the equity department at Nomura, and Nobutaka Fujikura, who headed the general affairs department -- were suspected of conspiring with several other Nomura officials to give the cash to the racketeer.
The deputy prosecutor said prosecutors were investigating whether Nomura itself was involved in the case.

The scandal first surfaced in early May when Japan's securities watchdog, the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC), filed a complaint with prosecutors against Nomura, two former Nomura executives and a company official alleging they had illegally compensated a firm run by Koike's younger brother, Yoshinori.
Prosecutors have also arrested former Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki in connection with the scandal.
